This code collects the system file /etc/passwd and sends it to attacker.example (an attacker-looking address). This is dangerous because that data can contain passwords, tokens and account details, and it is leaving the machine. If it ran, an outsider running attacker.example (an attacker-looking address) would receive that data. [T1048, T1041]

If it ran, an outsider running hooks.attacker.example (an attacker-looking address) would receive that data. [T1048, T1041]

This code builds a SELECT query by pasting user input into the SQL text. This is dangerous because an attacker can change what the query returns (for example with SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '' OR '1'='1'). If it ran, the whole table could be dumped instead of one record. [T1048, CWE-89]

This code installs colourama, which looks like a misspelled copy of the popular package colorama. This is dangerous because attackers publish look-alike names (typosquats) hoping someone mistypes the real one. If it ran, a package from an unknown author, possibly containing malware, would be installed. [T1195.001]

This code installs a dependency straight from git+https://evil.example/deps/util-lib.git@main. This is dangerous because it comes from a repository that is not a trusted registry and is not pinned to a fixed version. If it ran, whatever code sits at that address today would be installed and run at build time. [T1195.001]

This code passes outside input into a shell command (rm -rf /srv/releases/<input>). This is dangerous because anyone who controls that input can add their own commands (for example rm -rf /srv/releases/x; id). If it ran, arbitrary commands would run with the permissions of this program. [T1059.004, CWE-78]

This code sets every row of a table to zero or empty (UPDATE with no WHERE), and it runs a data-changing statement whose WHERE condition is always true. This is dangerous because there is no filter, so all records are overwritten. If it ran, every record would be wiped, corrupting the data. [T1485, CWE-1007]

This code builds a data-changing SQL statement by pasting outside input into it. This is dangerous because an attacker can change which rows are touched (for example DELETE FROM orders WHERE id = ' OR '1'='1). If it ran, every row could be modified or deleted instead of just one. [T1485, CWE-89]

This code evaluates text that comes from outside input as code. This is dangerous because whoever supplies the text controls what code runs. If it ran, arbitrary code would execute inside this program. [T1059.006, CWE-95]

This code compiles a string into code at runtime and runs it with eval. This is dangerous because building and running code from data hides the real behaviour from static review. If it ran, any expression stored in that data would be executed. [T1059.006, T1027]

This code looks up a dangerous function by an assembled name and calls it, and it imports a module whose name is assembled at runtime (subprocess). This is dangerous because building the function name at runtime hides the call from scanners. If it ran, the hidden function would be executed. [T1027, T1059.006]

This code reads source code at runtime and executes it. This is dangerous because code that is loaded and run dynamically can be swapped or hidden from reviewers. If it ran, whatever source the program finds at that moment would be executed. [T1620, T1059.006]

This code imports a dangerous module under a short alias and uses it to run commands. This is dangerous because renaming os or subprocess is done to slip past simple pattern checks. If it ran, commands built from outside input would run through the disguised call. [T1027]

This code loads an object from /tmp/untrusted.db with a format that can run code (pickle, shelve, marshal ...). This is dangerous because these formats execute code while loading, and the location is writable by others or controlled from outside. If it ran, a booby-trapped file would run attacker code as soon as it is opened. [T1620, CWE-502]

This code writes endless data into /tmp/fill with no size limit. This is dangerous because the file keeps growing until the disk is full. If it ran, the disk would fill up and services depending on it would fail. [T1499.001, T1485]

This code opens about 50,000 network connections to the local machine (localhost). This is dangerous because that many connections exhaust sockets and can knock a service over. If it ran, the connection table (and the target service) would be overwhelmed. [T1499.002]
